Definition: A proposed free and open-source, local-first, analysis-grade piping design engine with an integrated piping flexibility and stress-analysis core.
The software environment that applies design knowledge, physical modeling, constraints, analysis, comparison, and handoff workflows before professional validation.
An accepted industry-standard professional stress-analysis platform used by the responsible engineer to validate a design for project reliance.
User-supplied or organization-supplied information that informs model generation and evaluation.
The user's rich editable design model including geometry, components, supports, equipment interfaces, loads, materials, constraints, libraries, provenance, and unresolved assumptions.
The idealized piping flexibility/stress line-element model produced from the physical model and solved by the internal engine.
A target-specific representation exported from the physical and analytical models to feed downstream modeling and external professional stress-analysis tools.
A user- or organization-supplied artifact defining required inputs, stress categories, load-case mappings, expressions, allowables, checks, warnings, and blocking conditions.
A named, immutable snapshot of a model recording the physical model, analysis inputs, references, tags, notes, unresolved assumptions, and model hash.
A solver execution attached to a specific model state, recording solver version, settings, load cases, diagnostics, rule-pack and library references, and results.
A deterministic diff between two model states and/or two analysis runs using stable IDs, mappings, unit-normalized quantities, and tolerance profiles.
Evaluation of recorded results against user-supplied rules and data; not professional approval.
The six nodal freedoms (three translations and three rotations) supported at every active structural node.
User-supplied in-plane, out-of-plane, and torsional intensification factors applied to bends and branches.
Notes: Public project ships no protected B31J SIF data

Definition: User-supplied factors modifying element flexibility for bends and other components.
User-defined absolute and relative tolerances by result category used in comparison.
Exported schema-compliant model data and manifests intended for downstream modeling or professional stress-analysis workflows.
The design principle preserving the distinction between software-computed results and professional engineering acceptance.
Source and verification metadata recorded for materials, components, SIFs, allowables, rules, and library records.
A component supporting axial/lateral/angular/torsional stiffness, effective pressure area, pressure thrust, movement limits, and manufacturer provenance.
The engine that evaluates model consistency and project constraints such as connectivity, clearances, no-go volumes, and support zones.
Future capability proposing route/support alternatives as model operations constrained by the physical model, schema, design knowledge, and analytical results.
